issues.title: 5.19 lakh PV dispatches. Which cars have actually reached customers?
issues.summary: SIAM's 13 November statement reports 5,19,060 domestic passenger-vehicle manufacturer sales for October 2026. This factory-to-dealer wholesale measure, with specified brand exclusions, is not a count of customer deliveries or registrations. RPHV's operational response: test delivery readiness, parts and service handoffs, exchange risk and cash reconciliation against each VIN rather than reading national dispatches as dealer success.

The release quotes 5,19,060 PV units; its separately noted PV total without Tata Motors is 4,45,166 units. Two- and three-wheeler domestic sales are 25,77,810 and 1,03,349 units. These are not VAHAN/FADA retail registrations or verified dealership handovers.

intro: On 13 November 2026, the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) released its October 2026 performance statement. It reported 5,19,060 domestic passenger-vehicle sales, 25,77,810 two-wheeler sales and 1,03,349 three-wheeler sales. SIAM described passenger vehicles as up 12.4% from October 2025 and called October 2026 the segment's strongest October to date.

Read the measurement before the headline: SIAM's domestic-sales series records manufacturers' dispatches into the domestic trade, not completed customer registrations. Its passenger-vehicle headline includes Tata Motors in the public statement but excludes BMW, Mercedes, Jaguar Land Rover and Volvo Auto. The stated passenger-vehicle figure excluding Tata Motors is 4,45,166; that alternative coverage must never be compared casually with the headline total.

A dealer facing stronger arrivals should ask four separate questions: which units have identified customers; which are actually ready for handover; which leave an open exchange, accessory or service obligation; and which payments or credits remain unreconciled? A market-wide wholesale record is not evidence of a particular dealer's conversion rate, stock ageing or profit.

interpretation.heading: Replace the market headline with a VIN-level reality check
points: Review units due for delivery over the next seven days against actual customer commitment, finance, registration and accessory readiness; do not count an invoice as a completed handover.
Trace pending pre-delivery inspections, accessory fitment and service/parts promises to a named person and a credible customer update time.
Link delivered VINs to money: check customer receipts, bank disbursements, exchange settlements and manufacturer claims separately before treating sales volume as released cash.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Separate bookings, invoices and handovers
desks.check: Review the next seven calendar days' committed deliveries. For each VIN, confirm customer booking, allocation, finance approval, registration stage, accessory readiness and promised date.
desks.metric: VINs ready on all required gates / VINs committed for delivery within 7 days (%)
desks.rationale: Wholesale arrivals, bookings, invoices and actual handovers occur at different stages; separate them.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Close the PDI and early ownership handoff
desks.check: Check the next ten due deliveries for a signed PDI, cleared defects, new-owner orientation and recorded first-service contact.
desks.metric: Due deliveries with signed PDI and no unresolved safety hold / due deliveries checked (%)
desks.rationale: A customer should not receive a vehicle with unresolved readiness or safety exceptions.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Protect promised accessory fitment
desks.check: For every delivery requiring accessories this week, match the committed kit to VIN, physical stock and installer slot; flag unconfirmed supplier ETAs.
desks.metric: Accessory-requiring VINs with parts and fitment slot confirmed / accessory-requiring VINs due (%)
desks.rationale: A warehouse order is not a customer-ready accessory.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Keep exchange margins and ownership auditable
desks.check: For exchange deals supporting imminent new-car deliveries, verify RC/ownership, lien or hypothecation status, signed condition appraisal, reconditioning estimate and approved exchange price.
desks.metric: Exchange-linked deliveries with completed acquisition dossier / exchange-linked deliveries due (%)
desks.rationale: An apparently completed new-car deal may carry unresolved used-vehicle liabilities.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Verify cash release against the VIN
desks.check: For yesterday's delivered VINs, reconcile advance, final invoice, customer receipt, lender disbursement, exchange credit and any unpaid balance; assign owners to unmatched items.
desks.metric: Unreconciled value against delivered VINs older than 2 working days (₹)
desks.rationale: Increased dispatches or billed revenue are not the same as collected cash.

issues.huddleTitle: One VIN, five checkpoints, fifteen minutes
issues.huddleSummary: Select one customer delivery due within seven days, ideally with an exchange and accessory fitting. Spend three minutes per department and end with one verified Go/Hold decision, named owners and customer-update times.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — SALES: Show booking, exact VIN, promised delivery date, finance and registration position; identify missing evidence.
Minutes 3–6 — SERVICE: Confirm signed PDI status, defect closure and customer orientation responsibility; flag any safety hold.
Minutes 6–9 — SPARES: Match required accessories with physical stock, fitment booking and actual order status; separate estimate from confirmed ETA.
Minutes 9–12 — USED CARS: If a trade-in applies, verify ownership, hypothecation, condition and approved acquisition margin; otherwise review the next pending exchange.
Minutes 12–15 — ACCOUNTS: Reconcile receipts, loan payout and exchange adjustment; record Go/Hold, outstanding tasks, owners, deadlines and next customer update.
limitations: The source publication date is 13 November 2026; the reported domestic-sales period spans 1–31 October 2026. The issue date is 14 November 2026, not the event date.
SIAM numbers describe manufacturer domestic sales/wholesale dispatches, not retail registrations (FADA/VAHAN), invoices, deliveries, confirmed booking conversions or customer payment collections.

SIAM's PV headline includes Tata Motors only in this public release and excludes BMW, Mercedes, JLR and Volvo Auto. The release also provides a distinct 4,45,166 PV figure excluding Tata Motors; this is a different coverage basis and is not presented as a year-on-year comparator.
SIAM's overall production headline has a separate exclusion footnote that also excludes Tata Motors. Production is not used as a metric in this issue.

The release states PV growth of 12.4% versus October 2025, but this edition does not infer a dealership growth rate from it. No vehicle subsegment, geography-by-state or dealership profitability breakdown is claimed.

The source is an official public association release, not an independently audited dealer census. Numbers may be updated by the reporting association. Retail-registration estimates from other sources have not been combined because matching methodology and coverage were not verified in this editorial draft.
The five operational checks, sample sizes, deadlines and suggested KPI formulas are original RPHV management proposals, not SIAM or OEM standards.

issues.title: One roof, three functions. Is the customer journey joined up?
issues.summary: Stellantis opened an integrated Jeep and Citroën Sales, Service and Spares facility in Patna on 26 October 2026. A single site may simplify access, but a reliable customer experience requires connected records, accountable handoffs and visible exceptions across every desk—not just shared premises.

Approximately 19,000 sq. ft. describes premises area, six is showroom display capacity, and nine is workshop bay count. These are announced capacity figures, not units sold, retail registrations, throughput or independent quality results.

issues.reportingType: Single-location manufacturer-declared facility inauguration and physical capacity; NOT nationwide OEM wholesales, customer retail registrations, actual workshop throughput, sales conversions, audited financial performance or a survey.
intro: On 26 October 2026, Stellantis India announced the opening of its first Stellantis Brand House in Bihar with dealer partner KP Automobiles Pvt. Ltd. The integrated Jeep and Citroën facility at Ranipur Bypass, Patna brings Sales, Service and Spares (3S) under one roof. The company reported approximately 19,000 sq. ft. of space, including a showroom able to display six vehicles and a nine-bay workshop.

The company says the workshop is equipped for routine maintenance, mechanical repairs, wheel alignment and balancing, and accident and body-shop work. These are declared capabilities at launch, not independently measured repair completion times, parts-fill rates, customer satisfaction or revenue. The release does not establish what proportion of customers already use the combined location.

For dealership operators, the useful question is whether a shared address produces a shared customer record. A buyer's VIN, promised accessory, registration status, first-service date, complaint, parts order and settlement should be traceable without repeated calls between departments.

interpretation.heading: Integration is an operating discipline, not a building design
points: Assign one accountable owner for each pending customer promise, even where departments or brands share a site.
Use a VIN- or RO-linked exception log so Sales, Service, Spares and Accounts see the same agreed next action and deadline, within permitted access rights.
Measure actual service completion, parts readiness, customer communication and payment resolution before concluding that a 3S format improves performance.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Complete the post-sale handoff
desks.check: Review the last ten new-vehicle delivery files. Confirm VIN, accessory promises, service introduction, complaint contact and first-service reminder are recorded and handed over to the correct team.
desks.metric: Delivery files with complete aftersales handoff / delivery files checked (%)
desks.rationale: A co-located workshop cannot support the customer when ownership details and promises are missing.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Make each repair promise visible
desks.check: Review ten open ROs; confirm approved scope, technician or bay assignment, blocked status, promised completion time and next customer update.
desks.metric: Open ROs with a documented next update and accountable owner / open ROs reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: Nine physical bays measure installed space, not completed repairs or customer trust.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Link each parts promise to a real job
desks.check: Trace parts requirements on ten pending ROs to the correct VIN, brand catalogue, purchase/stock acknowledgement and dated availability commitment.
desks.metric: Parts-dependent ROs with confirmed fitment and ETA / parts-dependent ROs reviewed (%)
desks.rationale: An integrated store still requires traceable, brand-correct parts and realistic delivery dates.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Keep exchange commitments evidence-based
desks.check: For current exchange proposals, verify ownership, inspection, reconditioning costs and approved valuation before anyone promises an exchange price.
desks.metric: Exchange proposals with signed appraisal and cost sheet / exchange proposals assessed (%)
desks.rationale: A new-car sale should not conceal a future loss or ownership dispute on the trade-in.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Connect money to the same VIN or RO
desks.check: Match sampled customer advances, final invoices, approved accessories, repair bills and outstanding credits to the VIN or RO. Give unresolved cases named owners.
desks.metric: Value of cross-desk unreconciled items older than 2 working days (₹)
desks.rationale: Shared premises alone will not close financial exceptions or prevent unsupported handovers.

issues.huddleTitle: One customer, five desks, fifteen minutes
issues.huddleSummary: Trace one live vehicle journey across all five departments. Each gets three minutes. Finish with a single list of blockers, owners and next customer-update times.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — Sales: show the VIN, committed delivery and accessories, and the contact that owns the customer's relationship.
Minutes 3–6 — Service: locate any PDI, first service, complaint or open RO, with promised date and responsibility.
Minutes 6–9 — Spares: check any pending items by VIN and catalogue, with supplier acknowledgement and realistic ETA.
Minutes 9–12 — Used Cars: verify exchange appraisal and transfer file if there is a trade-in; otherwise select the next active exchange file.
Minutes 12–15 — Accounts: reconcile the advance, invoice and pending credits; name an owner and deadline for each remaining exception.
limitations: The primary source is dated 26 October 2026. This 13 November edition interprets an October inauguration; it does not report a new 13 November launch.

The approximately 19,000 sq. ft. site area, nine service bays and six displayed vehicles are announced physical capacities for one Patna facility. No service-jobs-per-day or sales-per-day denominator was supplied.

Jeep and Citroën share the announced facility, but the release does not establish identical service procedures, warranty policies or interchangeability of parts between brands. OEM-specific authorisations remain necessary.
The company also reports nationwide touchpoints and a 2026 network expansion, but those different date bases and counting units are deliberately excluded from this issue's visual metrics.
The release does not give independent customer-satisfaction outcomes, before-and-after repair turnaround, revenue, margin, network-wide uptake, or realised savings from co-location.

There are no manufacturer domestic-wholesale sales or retail-registration figures in this edition. All five departmental checks and metrics are original RPHV management proposals, not Stellantis standards or measured company results.

issues.title: Service is moving closer to the customer. Can the process follow?
issues.summary: Two Maruti Suzuki initiatives announced in 2026 show complementary directions in aftersales: small on-site service facilities at high-density locations and flexible prepaid maintenance. Neither announcement proves shorter repair times or better profitability. The dealership opportunity lies in clear job scope, scheduled capacity, parts readiness and reconciled package obligations.
issues.sourceNote: Maruti Suzuki Quickstop original corporate release dated 30 March 2026 (10 facilities in pilot locations at launch); Maruti Suzuki Smart Maintenance Plan original corporate release dated 15 June 2026 (customer offer terms as announced, not current sales volumes). This 12 November article is an operational analysis of earlier 2026 announcements, not a newly launched November programme.

metrics.context: Company-reported on 30 March 2026; located across eight listed markets/regions

issues.reportingType: Two dated OEM service-format/product announcements, NOT wholesale dispatches, retail vehicle registrations, workshop performance results, audited financial outcomes, survey results or proof of adoption.
intro: On 30 March 2026, Maruti Suzuki announced 'Quickstop', a compact modified-container service facility designed for routine maintenance and minor repairs at places such as corporate campuses, airport zones and fleet hubs. The company identified 10 pilot facilities across Delhi-NCR, Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Kolkata, Bagdogra, Calicut and Surat. Dealer partners operate the units while participating corporate entities or fleet operators provide the space.

On 15 June 2026, Maruti Suzuki separately introduced its Smart Maintenance Plan (SMP). Customers could select labour-only, parts-and-labour and other configurations; the company stated at least a 10% saving on labour under the plan, subject to terms. Published options extended up to 10 years/100,000 km for private vehicles, and up to 10 years/160,000 km for commercial vehicles. The plan is usable at authorised Maruti Suzuki dealer workshops across India.

Both releases describe propositions, not measured outcomes: neither source supplies a controlled comparison of repair turnaround, customer retention, number of prepaid-plan purchases or dealership operating margin. Their relevance to other dealers is as models to evaluate, not claims to copy verbatim.

interpretation.heading: The service promise needs an operating system
points: Choose a limited service menu and clearly separate on-site jobs from repairs requiring full workshop tools, diagnosis, safety controls or specialist technicians.
Offer an appointment only after checking location access, technician capacity, correct parts/consumables and a realistic return time; capture the customer's approval of extra work.
For prepaid packages, map covered and excluded items, eligibility, redemptions, workshop reimbursement and balances; measure economic outcomes before promising savings or scaling.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Explain service convenience without overpromising
desks.check: At delivery, record whether the customer received a correct explanation of available service channels, package eligibility, covered work and exclusions. Avoid suggesting another brand's offer applies to your dealership.
desks.metric: New deliveries with documented service-option briefing / new deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: A transparent, realistic convenience promise can support retention; unsupported claims create complaints.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Keep on-site scope and time promises credible
desks.check: For the next ten scheduled routine-service visits, verify work scope, bay or site capacity, technician allocation, ETA and out-of-scope referral route before confirmation.
desks.metric: Routine-service jobs completed within committed time / routine-service jobs completed (%)
desks.rationale: Convenience depends on a kept appointment and a safe handoff, not only proximity.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Pre-kit routine-service parts against VIN
desks.check: Match the next day's service appointments to VIN-correct filters, oil grade, consumables and supplier alternatives approved under OEM rules. Flag gaps before the customer arrives.
desks.metric: Booked routine-service appointments with full confirmed parts kit / total booked routine-service appointments (%)
desks.rationale: A nearby service location still fails the customer if the correct consumables are missing.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Disclose what service readiness means
desks.check: Before delivery of a pre-owned car, record completed maintenance, outstanding recommendations, service history and any plan or warranty eligibility validated with the issuer.
desks.metric: Used-car deliveries with signed maintenance-status disclosure / total used-car deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: Documented readiness protects trust without implying an unverified warranty or maintenance-plan transfer.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Keep package cash and obligations apart
desks.check: For every collected prepaid maintenance amount or partner reimbursement, reconcile receipt, package entitlement, job redemption and the agreed accounting treatment; flag unmatched items.
desks.metric: Unreconciled prepaid-service receipts and redemptions older than 7 days (₹)
desks.rationale: Upfront cash is not proof of earned service revenue or programme profitability.

issues.huddleTitle: One routine service, five checks, fifteen minutes
issues.huddleSummary: Use one real upcoming booked service or proposed fleet visit. Each team contributes a three-minute evidence check; conclude with a go/hold decision, owner and customer message.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — Sales: confirm customer promise, plan eligibility, service location and approved price explanation.
Minutes 3–6 — Service: decide whether the job is suitable for the intended site; identify technician, available slot and promised return time.
Minutes 6–9 — Spares: confirm VIN-linked consumables, correct oil grade, required stock and parts contingency.
Minutes 9–12 — Used Cars: if relevant, verify prior repair history and any unfulfilled maintenance before committing on the vehicle; otherwise check the next used-car delivery.
Minutes 12–15 — Accounts: verify billing/package status and advance reconciliation; assign one owner and deadline to each gap, then issue the final customer confirmation.
limitations: The Quickstop release was dated 30 March 2026, and the SMP release 15 June 2026. These are earlier-year developments analysed on 12 November, not new November launches.

The 10 Quickstop facilities are the company's pilot count at the March announcement; there is no verified November 2026 live-location total, utilisation rate, service-volume denominator or repair-turnaround reduction.

The 10%+ statement concerns advertised labour-cost savings for SMP subject to applicable terms, model, service and location. It must not be represented as an unconditional 10% discount on the entire invoice or a dealer profit figure.

Ten-year/100,000-km private and ten-year/160,000-km commercial options are described as maximum configurations, not automatically available to every vehicle; actual package eligibility and cost must be checked.
The Quickstop format targets routine and minor work, not all repairs; safety-critical, high-voltage or specialist work may need authorised full-workshop infrastructure.
Neither source reports customer registrations, manufacturer wholesale sales, independent satisfaction outcomes, controlled performance comparisons or actual programme margins.
The five operational checks and metrics are original RPHV recommendations and not Maruti Suzuki dealer standards or contractual terms. They require local policy and feasibility review.

issues.title: Five stars are not the whole story. Check the VIN.
issues.summary: Mahindra's XUV 3XO ZNG earned a five-star Bharat NCAP rating, but the assessment also carries an important vehicle-identification qualification. The customer deserves the correct variant, VIN-specific score and clearly explained safety equipment—not a generic showroom badge.
issues.sourceNote: Mahindra press release dated 6 November 2026; Bharat NCAP's XUV 3XO rating began in November 2024 and its official vehicle page records a November 2026 extension to CNG variants. Bharat NCAP specifies that the revised child-protection score of 45/49 applies to vehicles from VIN MA1NS2NVPS2B98575 onwards; earlier vehicles retain 43/49. The exact day of the Bharat NCAP website revision is not displayed.

issues.reportingType: Model-specific standardized Bharat NCAP crash-test rating and November 2026 applicability revision; NOT manufacturer wholesale dispatches, retail registrations, vehicle-sale totals or crash-outcome statistics
intro: On 6 November 2026, Mahindra announced that its factory-fitted CNG XUV 3XO ZNG had received five stars under Bharat NCAP, with 29.36 out of 32 points for Adult Occupant Protection and 45 out of 49 for Child Occupant Protection. These are defined crash-assessment scores, not a prediction of protection in every real-world collision.

The full story is more specific than the showroom headline. The official Bharat NCAP XUV 3XO vehicle page says the original rating was published in November 2024 and was extended to the CNG family in November 2026. It also states that the revised child-protection score of 45/49 is applicable only to vehicles built from VIN MA1NS2NVPS2B98575 onwards; vehicles before that VIN retain 43/49. Both reported score sets correspond to five-star child ratings.

That production-cutoff note matters whenever a salesperson discusses a rating, a customer compares variants or a used-car appraiser assesses an earlier vehicle. The right sales promise identifies the exact vehicle and official rating applicability before quoting the headline.

interpretation.heading: Turn a safety badge into an evidence-backed explanation
points: Use the vehicle's actual VIN, fuel type, variant and manufacture record to check the official assessment's applicability; never assume every car sharing a model name carries exactly the same published score.

Explain standard airbags, electronic stability control, ISOFIX availability and the manufacturer's CNG gas-leak protection using approved documentation, without promising that any vehicle is injury-proof.
Record which safety information was communicated to the buyer, and refer technical or CNG-system questions to the authorised manufacturer procedure rather than ad-hoc workshop checks.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Verify the car behind the claim
desks.check: Before quoting a Bharat NCAP result, match actual VIN, variant and fuel system with the current official ratings-applicability notes; retain that check in the delivery file.
desks.metric: Safety-rating claims supported by VIN and variant check ÷ safety-rating claims made (%)
desks.rationale: The published assessment can contain production-batch exclusions that a generic model brochure does not show.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Complete a safety-focused handover
desks.check: Document OEM-prescribed pre-delivery warning-lamp checks and explain seat-belt, ISOFIX and relevant CNG safety instructions; escalate CNG faults to trained authorised staff.
desks.metric: Deliveries with signed safety/PDI handover checklist ÷ deliveries due (%)
desks.rationale: A high crash-test rating does not replace functioning safety equipment and owner understanding.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Do not guess on safety-critical parts
desks.check: Verify safety-system and CNG-related part numbers against the exact VIN and OEM catalogue before ordering or issuing replacement parts.
desks.metric: Safety-critical part orders with verified VIN fitment ÷ all safety-critical part orders (%)
desks.rationale: Correct part selection matters more than quick but incorrect substitution.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Check rating and modifications separately
desks.check: During acquisition, record VIN, fuel system as originally manufactured, known safety-system repairs and any non-OEM CNG modification; verify whether the tested rating actually applies.
desks.metric: Used-car appraisals with VIN-linked safety and fuel-system record ÷ total appraisals (%)
desks.rationale: A used vehicle's actual specification and repair history may differ from the car described in a sales advertisement.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Make safety charges transparent
desks.check: Match billed safety accessories or child-restraint equipment against approved quotations, actual fitment and customer acknowledgement; flag unsupported safety-related charges.
desks.metric: Deliveries with safety-accessory bill-to-fitment reconciliation ÷ deliveries containing such items (%)
desks.rationale: Trust requires accurate invoices as well as accurate vehicle information.

issues.huddleTitle: Check one VIN before making a five-star claim
issues.huddleSummary: Use one live quotation or incoming used car. Each desk checks one part of the evidence chain. Finish with the approved claim, a gap owner and a customer update.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — Sales: identify actual VIN, variant and fuel type; check the rating's applicability and cutoff note.
Minutes 3–6 — Service: verify PDI record, warning indicators, seat-belt/ISOFIX explanation and appropriate CNG safety instructions.
Minutes 6–9 — Spares: confirm any safety-critical replacement item is matched to VIN and manufacturer catalogue.
Minutes 9–12 — Used Cars: review manufacturing specification, repairs and modifications that affect what can accurately be promised.
Minutes 12–15 — Accounts: reconcile billed safety items with approved scope; record 'claim verified', 'hold' or 'correct communication', an owner and deadline.
limitations: The 6 November 2026 manufacturer statement and official Bharat NCAP vehicle page concern a defined model and assessment; the results are not retail registrations, factory wholesales, sales performance, accident statistics or guarantees in real-world collisions.

Mahindra's five-star announcement is company communication. Bharat NCAP's official vehicle listing independently confirms the original November 2024 assessment, November 2026 CNG extension and VIN-specific child-score note. It does not display the exact day of its November 2026 revision.

The Bharat NCAP listing notes that the CNG AX5 underwent a frontal offset test while side and pole results were carried over because the body structure and safety systems remain the same. Do not imply each variant underwent every test independently.

Older XUV 3XO vehicles before VIN MA1NS2NVPS2B98575 retain a 43/49 COP score; 45/49 applies from that VIN onward. This issue makes no blanket claim that every XUV 3XO ever built has a 45/49 COP score.
Mahindra's claim to be the first sub-compact CNG SUV with five stars is deliberately not repeated: sub-segment definitions and rival applicability would need additional independent checking.
These five dealership checks and ratios are RPHV editorial recommendations, not Bharat NCAP test criteria, OEM operational standards or a substitute for approved service and safety procedures.

intro: Maruti Suzuki's October 2026 True Value anniversary announcement reports a 25-year pre-owned car business, more than 65 lakh cumulative vehicle sales since its 2001 launch, and 662 outlets across 338 cities. It describes vehicle assessment, documentation, history checks, certification and warranty support as part of its operating model.

These are company-reported business milestones, not sales achieved in October, not the number of unique Indian used-car buyers and not the size of the nationwide used-car market. The anniversary is a useful case study in process design, not proof that any certificate eliminates vehicle defects.

For dealerships of any brand, an inspection checklist is useful only if the recorded findings are supported by evidence, the reconditioning estimate is fully costed and the sale contract tells the buyer what is and is not covered. A glossy sales listing cannot replace a traceable vehicle file.

interpretation.heading: Build the proof before the promise
points: A buyer should be able to trace the VIN, registration details, prior ownership, known condition, service history and inspection findings to the actual vehicle.
Keep reconditioning costs, finance settlement, transfer documentation and warranty conditions visible to the decision-maker before the selling price is approved.
Treat digital listings and certification badges as invitations to inspect the evidence—not substitutes for the evidence itself.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Explain exactly what is included
desks.check: Before taking a used-car booking, show the written condition summary, disclosed exceptions, warranty scope and transfer responsibilities; record customer acknowledgement.
desks.metric: Used-car bookings with signed condition and terms disclosure ÷ total used-car bookings (%)
desks.rationale: A clear, documented promise helps prevent avoidable disputes after delivery.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Make inspections traceable
desks.check: For each car under appraisal, record VIN, inspection date, diagnostic findings, accident/flood indicators where assessable, road-test result and inspector sign-off.
desks.metric: Appraised cars with signed technical inspection ÷ cars appraised (%)
desks.rationale: A signed inspection captures known findings, not a guarantee against every hidden defect.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Cost the reconditioning properly
desks.check: Confirm VIN-correct replacement parts, prices and supplier availability for the approved reconditioning work before the purchase price is finalised.
desks.metric: Acquisition proposals with verified reconditioning parts cost and ETA ÷ total proposals (%)
desks.rationale: Unavailable or expensive parts can erase expected margin.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Close the ownership evidence gap
desks.check: Match RC and VIN to the physical vehicle; document ownership, finance/hypothecation status and the applicable transfer process before releasing acquisition payment.
desks.metric: Acquisitions with complete ownership and transfer dossier before payment ÷ total acquisitions (%)
desks.rationale: Acquisition without clean documents can delay legal transfer and resale.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Approve the all-in margin
desks.check: Sign off the price sheet including acquisition, finance settlement, repairs, logistics, statutory/transfer charges and estimated holding costs.
desks.metric: Acquisitions with approved all-in margin sheet ÷ total acquisitions (%)
desks.rationale: Gross selling spread is not the same as realised margin.

issues.huddleTitle: Can we prove this car is ready to sell?
issues.huddleSummary: Pick one vehicle being acquired or listed. Each department has three minutes to identify one missing piece of evidence; finish with a hold-or-release decision and owners.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — Sales: state the buyer-facing promise and identify anything not yet disclosed.
Minutes 3–6 — Service: show signed inspection findings and any unresolved technical risk.
Minutes 6–9 — Spares: verify parts needed for rectification and their confirmed cost/ETA.
Minutes 9–12 — Used Cars: check RC/VIN, finance status, transfer papers and outstanding approvals.
Minutes 12–15 — Accounts: confirm all-in margin and record 'ready', 'hold' or 'decline', plus the action owner.
limitations: The 65-lakh-plus figure is a cumulative company statement since 2001, not October 2026 sales, VAHAN registrations, unique people, or a measure of all Indian used-car transactions.
662 outlets and 338 cities describe a single company's reported network at its October 2026 announcement, not the total number of used-car dealers in India.

The corporate web page does not visibly print a release date in the retrieved text. Contemporary reports identify 16 October 2026; original timestamp or downloadable press release remains a final pre-publication verification task.

The standing Parivahan guidance for normal ownership transfers refers to Forms 29/30 and state-dependent documents and timelines. Dealers must confirm current requirements with their relevant RTO; no universal completion time is claimed.

These five checks and performance metrics are RPHV editorial suggestions, not manufacturer or government benchmarks. No evidence is presented that certification guarantees defect-free vehicles or higher realised margins.

intro: On 18 September 2026, Honda Cars India announced the ground-breaking of Phase II of its spare-parts warehouse at Doddaballapura near Bengaluru. The company said the planned addition would cover approximately 80,000 square metres with an investment of ₹450 crore. It projects 140,000 square metres of total site area after the expansion, including the 60,000-square-metre first phase operational since June 2025.

This is a useful example of investment in India's automotive aftersales supply chain, not evidence that service parts are arriving faster today. The stated hub serves the company's car, two-wheeler and power-products businesses. The release does not provide a completion date, order-fill rate, transit-time improvement or local-dealership result.

For managers, the actionable question is narrower: for each vehicle held up by a part, does someone know the correct part number, actual order status, dated supplier ETA, assigned owner and next customer update?

interpretation.heading: The last mile matters more than the headline
points: Separate stock at the central warehouse from stock available to your specific workshop; availability is not a promise until an order and delivery date are confirmed.
Make parts-blocked repair orders visible each morning. Record VIN, part number, supplier acknowledgement, ETA, escalation owner and customer update time.
Use scheduled repairs and actual fast-moving consumption to plan genuine demand. Avoid speculative buying that turns working capital into ageing inventory.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Protect accessory-ready deliveries
desks.check: For the next seven days' planned vehicle handovers, verify VIN-specific accessories and fitment slots before confirming the delivery time.
desks.metric: Deliveries with required accessories physically ready ÷ all deliveries requiring accessories (%)
desks.rationale: Do not equate a parts order with fitted accessories.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Keep parts-blocked ROs in sight
desks.check: Review every open repair order stopped by unavailable parts; confirm its age, revised promise and next customer-update owner.
desks.metric: Open parts-blocked ROs older than 48 hours (number)
desks.rationale: The customer needs a dependable next update even when the part is unavailable.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Know which ETA is confirmed
desks.check: Check the ten most urgent unfulfilled parts requests for VIN fitment, supplier acknowledgement, order status and a dated ETA.
desks.metric: Open parts orders with a supplier-confirmed ETA ÷ all open parts orders (%)
desks.rationale: An estimated arrival date without supplier acknowledgement is still a risk, not a delivery commitment.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Price reconditioning delays
desks.check: Before accepting an exchange vehicle, verify cost and availability of critical repair parts, including delayed or discontinued items.
desks.metric: Acquired used vehicles with parts-verified reconditioning sheets ÷ total acquired used vehicles (%)
desks.rationale: Low acquisition price cannot protect margin when essential parts are unavailable.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Unblock parts-related cash
desks.check: Match supplier advances and payments against purchase orders, invoices and goods received notes; flag amounts against unreceived items.
desks.metric: Unmatched parts-supplier advances older than 7 calendar days (₹)
desks.rationale: Paid does not mean received, and received does not mean correctly issued.

issues.huddleTitle: One missing part. Five decisions. Fifteen minutes.
issues.huddleSummary: Choose one actual parts-blocked repair order and use five three-minute reviews to resolve availability, fitment, customer promise, reconditioning exposure and cash.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 | Service: Explain the blocked RO, promised date and last customer update.
Minutes 3–6 | Spares: Verify exact part, supplier order status and dated ETA; flag unconfirmed information.
Minutes 6–9 | Sales: Check whether the issue also affects a planned new-car or accessory delivery.
Minutes 9–12 | Used Cars: Check whether the same part could delay an exchange-vehicle reconditioning job.
Minutes 12–15 | Accounts: Confirm any advance exposure, assign owners and schedule next customer/management update.
limitations: The 18 September 2026 company release is a project announcement, not a report from 9 November 2026; the newsletter date is the publication date of RPHV commentary.
Phase II had only reached the announced ground-breaking stage. The cited ₹450 crore and 80,000 m² refer to planned investment and addition, not completed assets or verified expenditure.
The 140,000 m² is the company's projected combined facility area after Phase II; 60,000 m² Phase I was reported operational in June 2025.
The company release gives no actual fill-rate, repair turnaround, delivery lead-time, opening/completion date or proof of dealer-level improvement.
The source is specific to one supplier network; the five checks are brand-neutral RPHV recommendations, not company performance targets. No vehicle wholesale or retail registrations are reported.

issues.reportingType: India October 2026 retail registrations (RTO-based); FADA national passenger-vehicle channel inventory-day estimate; forward-looking FADA dealer survey. NOT factory wholesales or dealership audited financial data.
intro: FADA's 6 November report places October 2026 passenger-vehicle retail registrations at 5,07,768 and estimates channel inventory at around 43–45 days, unchanged from September. The registrations reflect vehicles recorded at RTOs; the inventory-day figure is an association-level stock estimate. These are different measures, and neither shows the cash available in a particular dealership.

Looking ahead, 51.65% of respondents to FADA's Online Members' Survey expected retail growth in November. That is sentiment, not a forecast guaranteed to come true. With Diwali on 8 November, the test for a dealer is whether scheduled handovers become completed, correctly accounted transactions.

A vehicle can have a customer invoice, a registration entry and a promised delivery without every supporting receipt, bank payout, exchange adjustment or credit note being reconciled. The useful festive-season control is a short, daily exception list: which unit is still in stock, who owes which amount and who owns the next action?

interpretation.heading: Turn festive activity into reconciled business
points: Separate three records in the daily review: OEM-to-dealer dispatches (wholesale), customer registrations (retail), and actual dealership receipts. Reconcile differences instead of treating them as interchangeable sales figures.
Age each unsold vehicle and record its landed cost and funding status; do not apply the nationwide 43–45-day estimate to any individual stock ledger.

Close the handover loop: finance disbursement, customer balance, exchange adjustment, accessory bill and delivery acknowledgement must be traceable to the same vehicle/VIN. Track unresolved items by owner and date.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Check each promised handover
desks.check: From today's delivery list, match VIN, customer invoice, registration status, lender approval and payment clearance before confirming handover.
desks.metric: Delivery files with verified clearance ÷ deliveries scheduled today (%)
desks.rationale: A delivery promise should be supported by a complete customer and payment record.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Close PDI exceptions before release
desks.check: For each vehicle marked ready for delivery, confirm signed pre-delivery inspection and closure or authorised escalation of any open defect.
desks.metric: Planned deliveries with signed, cleared PDI ÷ planned deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: A last-minute repair hold is easier to manage when visible to Sales and Accounts.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Match accessories to the invoice
desks.check: Review billed accessories on today's handover list and confirm fitment, issue records and approved exceptions with Sales.
desks.metric: Billed accessory lines without verified fitment or issue (count)
desks.rationale: A missing accessory can delay handover or create avoidable billing disputes.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Record the full exchange adjustment
desks.check: For each exchange attached to a new delivery, verify acquisition value, existing loan closure/no-dues status, ownership documents and ledger treatment.
desks.metric: Exchange-linked deliveries with approved settlement sheet ÷ exchange-linked deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: Unresolved loans and undocumented offsets make the sale harder to reconcile.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Trace the money vehicle by vehicle
desks.check: Match each delivered VIN to customer receipts, lender disbursement, exchange offsets, taxes and any OEM receivable; assign ageing and owner to mismatches.
desks.metric: Unreconciled delivery-linked balance aged over 2 working days (₹)
desks.rationale: Completed deliveries are not the same as fully settled or reconciled transactions.

issues.huddleTitle: One VIN. Five checks. Fifteen minutes.
issues.huddleSummary: Select one live festive handover at risk. Spend three minutes with each desk, capture the gap and end with one named owner per unresolved item.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — SALES: Show the VIN, customer promise, invoice and payment/registration status.
Minutes 3–6 — SERVICE: Confirm signed PDI or identify the release blocker.
Minutes 6–9 — SPARES: Confirm accessories billed, issued and fitted.
Minutes 9–12 — USED CARS: If an exchange is involved, confirm loan settlement and adjustment documentation; otherwise record no exchange.
Minutes 12–15 — ACCOUNTS: Match bank receipts and lender payout to the VIN; assign owners and deadlines for every exception.
limitations: Original October 2026 FADA-hosted report/PDF was not accessible during research; the 6 November statement was checked through a separately hosted attributed reproduction and credible independent reports. The association's publicly visible LinkedIn feed corroborates the 43–45-day stock statement and 51.65% November sentiment, but exact first-party PDF footnotes remain unchecked. Do not publish until reconciled.
FADA's ~43–45 inventory days describe the passenger-vehicle channel at an industry level, not an audited figure for an individual dealership or a rupee financing cost.

51.65% is the share of respondents to a FADA Online Members' Survey expecting growth in November 2026. Survey sample size, response rate and full questionnaire were not verified; it is not a measure of realised sales or a probability.

October 2026 retail registrations are not manufacturer-to-dealer dispatches (wholesales). The festive calendar differs from October 2025 because Diwali is in November 2026; simple annual comparisons can mislead.
The recommended checks and two-working-day exception threshold are RPHV editorial management suggestions, not FADA, OEM, RBI or statutory norms.

issues.reportingType: FADA-reported retail registrations for 1–31 October 2026; not manufacturer wholesales, workshop inflow, or a dealer-level survey
intro: The number worth noticing is not a workshop target. FADA's 6 November 2026 statement says electric-vehicle retail registrations reached approximately 3.55 lakh across vehicle categories in October 2026. Within passenger vehicles, electric models represented 7.30% of 5,07,768 retail registrations. These are two different denominators.

A registered vehicle is not a service visit. It would be misleading to turn a month's EV retail data into a forecast for service revenue, trained-technician demand or diagnostic failures. But the changing mix is a useful reason to audit how enquiries and repair orders are received, identified and handed to the right people.

For the next EV or hybrid customer, can the advisor capture the exact vehicle and complaint, can the workshop assign work only within its training and equipment limits, and can the customer get a realistic update? That is the operational test, not a slogan about electrification.

interpretation.heading: Prepare the service process before the next exception
points: Identify the powertrain and exact vehicle/VIN at appointment and job-card creation; do not treat EV, hybrid and conventional vehicles as interchangeable.

For work involving high-voltage systems, follow the manufacturer procedure and route only to authorised, appropriately trained personnel; escalate otherwise. This is a safety and process recommendation, not a claim about an industry-wide skills gap.
Agree on parts availability, diagnostic authorisation, expected completion and next customer-update time before making a delivery promise.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Explain ownership support at handover
desks.check: For each EV delivery, verify that the customer receives model-specific charging, roadside assistance, warranty and service-booking guidance.
desks.metric: EV deliveries with recorded customer orientation ÷ EV deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: A useful handover reduces avoidable confusion over whom to contact for help.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Route the job to the right technician
desks.check: Review electrified-vehicle job cards for VIN/powertrain identification, a named trained owner and safe escalation where high-voltage competence or equipment is unavailable.
desks.metric: EV/hybrid ROs with documented qualified assignment and triage ÷ EV/hybrid ROs (%)
desks.rationale: Good routing protects safety and reduces unowned diagnostic delays.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Confirm fitment before quoting
desks.check: For an electrified-vehicle parts request, match VIN and part number and record availability, supersession and supplier ETA before promising completion.
desks.metric: EV/hybrid parts requests with verified VIN and ETA ÷ EV/hybrid parts requests (%)
desks.rationale: A wrong or delayed component can keep a specialist bay occupied.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Document battery and warranty evidence
desks.check: Before acquiring a used EV, record the VIN, warranty eligibility, charging accessories and an OEM-supported battery assessment where available.
desks.metric: Used EV appraisals with battery/warranty evidence ÷ used EV appraisals (%)
desks.rationale: Unknown battery or warranty status makes an appraisal unnecessarily speculative.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Track outstanding electrified-vehicle claims
desks.check: Review EV/hybrid warranty claims for complete invoices, approvals, labour documentation and payment status; assign owners to overdue cases.
desks.metric: Value of EV/hybrid warranty claims outstanding over 30 days (₹)
desks.rationale: Correct technical work still needs timely claim documentation and reconciliation.

issues.huddleTitle: One electrified-vehicle case. Five clean handoffs.
issues.huddleSummary: Use one real EV or hybrid case; if none is currently open, use the latest genuine customer enquiry. Record an owner, the next step and a deadline; never perform high-voltage work as part of the huddle.
huddle: Minutes 0–3: Sales checks what ownership, warranty and service guidance the customer received.
Minutes 3–6: Service confirms VIN, complaint, trained assignment and any safety/escalation limit.
Minutes 6–9: Spares validates any requested part number, fitment and availability.
Minutes 9–12: Used Cars checks what evidence would be needed if this vehicle came in for exchange.
Minutes 12–15: Accounts checks claim/billing documentation and the team records one owner, deadline and customer update.
limitations: FADA's statement, dated 6 November 2026, concerns October 1–31 retail registrations. No November registrations, future sales or aftersales RO volumes are inferred.
The approximately 3.55 lakh EV figure covers all vehicle categories. The 7.30% EV figure is a share of PASSENGER-VEHICLE retail registrations; the percentages are not interchangeable.

The October release was not available as a directly inspected PDF on the FADA domain (site access blocked); its FADA-authored statement was checked in a syndicated reproduction and its major figures corroborated by independent dated trade coverage. Original publisher-hosted document and RTO scope/coverage footnotes remain unverified; retain an approval hold.
Monthly retail-registration figures are not manufacturer wholesale dispatches, billings, cash collections, service visits, repair demand or evidence of staff competency gaps.
FADA attributes the October 2026 year-on-year comparison to the unusual festival calendar; this issue does not infer a measured service-workload effect.

All five desk checks and suggested metrics are original RPHV guidance, not FADA standards or mandatory manufacturer service procedures. Follow the applicable OEM safety directions; do not attempt high-voltage work without appropriate training/authorisation.
If no relevant EV/hybrid cases occurred, record the metric as not applicable, not 100%.

intro: The headline depends on the comparison chosen. In its 21 October release, FADA recorded 1,82,728 passenger-vehicle registrations during Navratri 2026 (11-20 October). That was 10.39% above the 1,65,534 registrations recorded across the ten-day 2024 Navratri period, yet 21.91% below the 2,34,004 recorded during Navratri 2025.

The 2025 festival window ran for eleven days (22 September-2 October), compared with ten days in 2026 and 2024. FADA also identified the September 2025 GST changes and accumulated demand as factors that made last year's base unusual. The reported decline should therefore not be treated as a clean measure of weakened customer interest.

For a dealership, the more useful question is operational: Of customers promising a festive delivery, how many cars are allocated, finance-cleared, registered and actually ready to hand over? Review that chain before changing discounts, staffing or purchase decisions. Registrations reflect retail activity; OEM dispatches are a different data series.

interpretation.heading: Read the market. Then inspect your own funnel.
points: Compare matched days or clearly label uneven festival windows; also examine the same dealership's week-by-week enquiry, booking and delivery stages.
For the coming seven days, verify every promised delivery against vehicle allocation, finance status, registration and required fitments. A booking is not a confirmed handover.
Record why each deferred delivery slipped: customer request, allocation, documents, finance, PDI or accessories. The reason tells managers which process to improve.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Check the promised delivery, not just the booking
desks.check: For all deliveries promised within seven days, confirm the customer's date, available VIN, finance approval and registration progress.
desks.metric: Fully confirmed deliveries ÷ deliveries promised in next 7 days (%)
desks.rationale: This identifies promises at risk without confusing industry registrations with your own sales funnel.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Release cars only after PDI closure
desks.check: Match every planned handover VIN to a completed pre-delivery inspection and closure of any safety or functional defects.
desks.metric: Deliveries with completed, signed PDI ÷ total deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: An incomplete inspection can turn a festive delivery into an early complaint.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Flag accessories holding up handovers
desks.check: Review accessories and fitments promised for the next seven days; verify kit availability, technician slot and supplier ETA.
desks.metric: Deliveries with all promised accessories ready before handover ÷ deliveries requiring accessories (%)
desks.rationale: Missing fitments create preventable delays and broken customer commitments.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Close exchange appraisals before the delivery date
desks.check: Identify upcoming deliveries with exchange commitments; confirm physical appraisal, ownership paperwork and approved trade-in value.
desks.metric: Exchange-linked deliveries with signed-off appraisals ÷ exchange-linked deliveries due (%)
desks.rationale: Unresolved exchange values can prevent a confirmed new-vehicle handover.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Clear money and documents before release
desks.check: Reconcile advances, lender payout confirmation, invoice balance and statutory charges on each delivery-due file.
desks.metric: Scheduled deliveries fully payment-cleared before handover ÷ scheduled deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: A delivery is operationally complete only when financial and documentation controls are clear.

issues.huddleTitle: Five desks. One delivery at risk. Fifteen minutes.
issues.huddleSummary: Use one real delivery file to identify the single blocker that could disappoint the customer, then assign its owner and deadline.
huddle: Minutes 0-3: Sales checks customer commitment, allocation and confirmed date.
Minutes 3-6: Service validates the VIN's PDI and any open defect.
Minutes 6-9: Spares confirms accessories, fitment slot and any part ETA.
Minutes 9-12: Used Cars clears exchange valuation and transfer paperwork, if applicable.
Minutes 12-15: Accounts confirms payment and registration-related clearance; record the owner and customer update time.
limitations: FADA's 21 October report was provisional. Retail data were collated as of 21 October 2026 from 1,468 of 1,469 RTOs in collaboration with MoRTH; figures can change with late registrations or revisions.

The festival windows differ: 2026 (11-20 Oct, 10 days), 2025 (22 Sep-2 Oct, 11 days), 2024 (3-12 Oct, 10 days). The -21.91% 2025 comparison is not a like-for-like daily or calendar-month growth measure.

FADA notes that Telangana registration data for 3W, CV and tractor categories were unavailable for Navratri 2026; this caveat applies to relevant all-vehicle totals, though PV is not listed among the missing categories.

FADA's discussion of GST-linked pent-up demand is industry interpretation, not causal proof about every dealership. Festival registrations cannot establish dealership enquiry conversion or profitability.

This article contains no October 2026 full-month FADA retail figure. It does not combine festival retail registrations with October manufacturer wholesale dispatches as if they describe the same period.
The five practical checks, metrics and 15-minute huddle are original RPHV operational suggestions, not FADA or OEM performance standards.

issues.title: The aftermarket is growing. Is the right part on your shelf?
issues.summary: ACMA reports a 9% increase in India's domestic auto-component aftermarket in FY2025-26. For dealerships, bigger industry demand is no substitute for correct part identification, reliable order ETAs and disciplined inventory.
issues.sourceNote: ACMA's FY2025-26 industry review is listed in its official press archive on 17 July 2026; figures cross-checked against ACMA's undated live industry summary. Reporting period: 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026. These are component-industry value indicators, not vehicle wholesales or retail registrations.

issues.reportingType: Auto-component industry value data, not vehicle wholesales or customer registrations
intro: India's auto-component business is expanding. ACMA reports that domestic aftermarket value grew 9% in FY2025-26 compared with FY2024-25, while total auto-component industry turnover grew 12.7%. ACMA also identifies EV components, excluding lithium-ion batteries, as 4.6% of domestic OEM component supplies.

These numbers have different denominators. The aftermarket figure is about replacement-parts market value; the 12.7% figure is about the wider components industry; the EV share refers to original-equipment component supplies. None measures dealer fill rate, repair delays, vehicle dispatches or retail registrations.

That distinction matters. A parts counter can be busy yet lose time and money through wrong variants, old superseded numbers, unconfirmed arrival dates and stock that never turns. Growth creates opportunity; process determines whether a workshop captures it.

interpretation.heading: Do not turn market growth into blind reordering
points: Build stock decisions from local repair history, model and powertrain mix, and actual demand—not an industry growth percentage.
Use VIN-based part identification, supersession checks and confirmed supplier lead times before promising completion dates.
Separate fast-moving service parts from high-value, low-frequency components so both customer waiting time and working capital remain visible.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Capture the exact vehicle variant
desks.check: Check five recent deliveries for complete VIN, model, year and powertrain details in the service/CRM record.
desks.metric: Delivery records with complete vehicle identification / deliveries checked (%)
desks.rationale: Accurate vehicle data reduces avoidable part-selection mistakes later.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Find the repairs stalled for parts
desks.check: Review parts-blocked repair orders; confirm part number, revised ETA, customer update and responsible person.
desks.metric: Open repair orders blocked for parts for over 48 hours (count)
desks.rationale: The 48-hour trigger is a suggested local escalation threshold, not an OEM standard.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Verify before you reorder
desks.check: Audit ten live parts orders against VIN/catalogue fitment, supersession, quantity and supplier confirmation.
desks.metric: Wrong-part returns / total parts issues in the review period (%)
desks.rationale: Correct fitment and first-time fill are more useful than ordering faster.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Cost variant-specific repairs early
desks.check: Before purchasing an exchange car, validate availability and price of required reconditioning parts.
desks.metric: Acquired units with signed, costed reconditioning sheets / acquired units (%)
desks.rationale: A cheap acquisition can become costly when repair parts are unavailable.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Trace money paid for parts not received
desks.check: Match supplier advances against open purchase orders, receipts and promised delivery dates.
desks.metric: Value of supplier advances for parts pending over 7 days (₹)
desks.rationale: A seven-day ageing flag is a management prompt, not a statutory threshold.

issues.huddleTitle: One delayed part. Five clear decisions.
issues.huddleSummary: Pick one real parts-blocked job. In 15 minutes, identify the fitment evidence, ETA, customer commitment and financial exposure.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — Sales: confirm VIN, model, powertrain and customer commitment.
Minutes 3–6 — Service: confirm symptom, diagnosis, part need and revised repair promise.
Minutes 6–9 — Spares: validate part number, supersession, stock and supplier ETA.
Minutes 9–12 — Used Cars: check whether any affected exchange/refurbishment job needs the same part and price update.
Minutes 12–15 — Accounts: confirm advance/credit exposure; assign the final owner and update deadline.

No October 2026 vehicle wholesale or retail-registration total is cited. No industry metric predicts a specific dealership's parts demand, customer waiting time or profitability.

issues.title: Record dispatches. What has actually turned into cash?
issues.summary: October's manufacturer sales releases show strong vehicle movement. But a wholesale headline is not a dealership's retail registration, stock turn or bank balance. This week's most useful question is which vehicles, repair jobs and claims have genuinely converted into collected money.
issues.sourceNote: Original Maruti Suzuki press release dated 1 November 2026 and Mahindra newsroom release page dated 2 November 2026 (its text carries a 1 November dateline), both reporting October 2026 manufacturer sales. These are company-reported dispatch/sales figures—not nationwide retail registrations, dealer deliveries or dealer cash receipts.

metrics.context: October 2026; includes domestic sales, sales to other OEMs and exports; OEM-reported

issues.reportingType: Two manufacturers' October 2026 sales/dispatch releases (wholesale-related data); NOT customer retail registrations or nationwide market totals.
intro: Two fresh October releases offer a useful lesson in reading automotive numbers. Maruti Suzuki reported total vehicle sales of 2,76,120 units: 2,16,789 domestic sales (including its light commercial vehicles), 9,459 units supplied to other OEMs and 49,872 exports. Mahindra reported 73,338 domestic utility-vehicle sales in the same month. These are different company-specific categories; they must not be added together or treated as India's retail registrations.

For a dealer, the gap between manufacturer billing and customer delivery matters more than the size of a market headline. Vehicles can arrive, create inventory and financing exposure, and still wait for documentation, loan clearance, accessories or final settlement. Similarly, a closed repair order or a manufacturer claim is not cash until its billing and collection are reconciled.

Use the next quarter-hour to compare what was billed, what was delivered and what was collected. If any figure is missing, assign an owner to close that gap rather than debating whether the market is strong.

interpretation.heading: The operating lesson: build a stock-to-cash bridge
points: Keep OEM wholesale invoices, dealer retail registrations, physical deliveries and customer receipts in separate columns. They record different events and often different dates.
Identify vehicles with invoices or stock funding already booked but delivery or payment still pending. Separate genuine bottlenecks from paperwork delays.
Run the same exception discipline through open repair orders, ordered parts, exchange-car acquisition costs and unsettled claims. Report the number and age of exceptions, not just gross turnover.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Reconcile every promised handover
desks.check: Review the next seven days' vehicle deliveries: confirm allocation, registration, payment clearance and handover documents against the promised date.
desks.metric: Delivery-ready units / units promised for next 7 days (%)
desks.rationale: An allocated or invoiced vehicle has not necessarily reached the customer.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Stop completed jobs waiting for billing
desks.check: Check completed repair orders not yet invoiced or delivered; identify missing final QC, approvals or customer communication.
desks.metric: Completed ROs awaiting invoice or delivery over 24 hours (count)
desks.rationale: Workshop productivity is only one step toward realised revenue.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Match inventory to real job demand
desks.check: Take the top five high-value parts purchased but not issued and verify each job reservation, physical location and expected use date.
desks.metric: Unissued purchased-parts value older than 30 days (₹)
desks.rationale: Paid-for stock without a defined job can quietly absorb cash.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Know total cost before listing
desks.check: Check one exchange vehicle's agreed purchase value, transfer papers, repair estimate, carrying cost and approved asking price.
desks.metric: Acquired cars with complete cost-and-margin sheet / total acquired cars (%)
desks.rationale: A healthy resale price is not automatically a healthy gross margin.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Show cash gaps by owner and age
desks.check: Reconcile yesterday's vehicle receipts, workshop collections, unsettled OEM claims and stock-funding debits; allocate every unmatched item.
desks.metric: Unreconciled receipts and claims over 7 days (₹)
desks.rationale: A visible pending balance can be followed up before it becomes an ageing problem.

issues.huddleTitle: From invoice to bank: close five gaps
issues.huddleSummary: Five desks each bring one real exception. Record the amount or vehicle/RO number, the blocker, an accountable person and a dated next action.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — Sales: pick one billed or allocated vehicle with delayed delivery; identify the exact blocker.
Minutes 3–6 — Service: pick one completed but unbilled RO; agree the next step and responsible person.
Minutes 6–9 — Spares: identify one paid-for part not issued to its intended job; confirm its status.
Minutes 9–12 — Used Cars: review one exchange vehicle with unapproved reconditioning cost or margin.
Minutes 12–15 — Accounts: reconcile one unmatched receipt or ageing claim and set a deadline.
limitations: The two OEM releases cover October 1–31, 2026 manufacturer-reported sales. They do not report VAHAN customer retail registrations, dealer delivery counts or dealer cash collections. No October nationwide retail-registration total is asserted.
Maruti Suzuki's 2,76,120 total contains exports (49,872), supplies to other OEMs (9,459), and domestic PV/LCV sales (2,16,789). It is not domestic passenger-car retail.

Mahindra's 73,338 figure is domestic utility vehicles, including its EV subsidiary; the company's broader 1,31,109 total spans other vehicle categories and exports. These scopes cannot be directly compared with Maruti's total or summed as an industry total.
Mahindra's newsroom page displays a publication date of 2 November 2026, while the release text is dated 1 November 2026. Both dates are disclosed rather than silently harmonised.

The five checks, metrics and 15-minute exercise are RPHV editorial recommendations, not OEM statistics, official benchmarks or a projection of profitability. Stock ageing cut-offs are practical local management choices, not industry standards.

issues.summary: An Indian commercial-vehicle maker has launched an AI-enabled service coordination system. The lesson for every dealership is practical: make each repair's next action, owner and promised time visible before buying another dashboard.
issues.sourceNote: VECV / Eicher Power Solutions announcement dated 13 October 2026. Company-reported connected-platform counts at the time of announcement; no monthly measurement window stated. This is NOT wholesale dispatch data or retail registrations.

issues.reportingType: Company product-launch announcement and self-reported platform scale; neither OEM wholesales nor customer retail registrations.
intro: On 13 October 2026, VE Commercial Vehicles announced an expanded AI-enabled uptime service model for its Eicher trucks and buses. It described a central control tower for service coordination and a generative-AI tool intended to help mechanics and diagnostic teams.

The company also reported that its My Eicher app supports more than 200,000 customers and connects over 460,000 vehicles. These are company-stated platform totals, not an independent survey, vehicle sales figures or proof that workshop turnaround has improved.

The useful dealership question is simple: can an adviser, technician, parts executive and customer all see who must do what next on a delayed job? Better visibility, clear ownership and timely escalation are worth testing before a costly technology rollout.

interpretation.heading: The operational lesson: close the handoff gap
points: Start with delayed or repeat repair orders. Record the current block, next action, accountable person and promised update time in one visible place.
Use diagnostic help tools to assist trained technicians, not to bypass manufacturer procedures, safety precautions or technical verification.
Measure first-time-right results and communication reliability before attributing improvements to AI. The announcement does not disclose audited changes in these outcomes.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Complete the after-sales handover
desks.check: Check five recent deliveries: was the customer shown how to book service, report a concern and reach roadside support where provided?
desks.metric: Deliveries with documented service onboarding / total deliveries (%)
desks.rationale: Ownership support should be clear before the first problem arises.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Give every blocked repair one owner
desks.check: Review five delayed or repeat-concern ROs; log the next action, named owner, customer-update deadline and escalation path.
desks.metric: Open ROs with owner + next action + update time / all open ROs (%)
desks.rationale: A dashboard cannot rescue a job nobody owns.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Replace vague parts status with evidence
desks.check: For each parts-blocked RO, record verified part number, order status, supplier confirmation and realistic ETA.
desks.metric: Parts-blocked ROs with confirmed status and ETA / all parts-blocked ROs (%)
desks.rationale: A credible ETA makes service promises more dependable.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Carry repair history into appraisal
desks.check: Check whether trade-in inspection records include warning lamps, diagnosis, pending repairs and realistic reconditioning cost.
desks.metric: Appraisals with complete diagnostic and repair-cost sheet / appraisals (%)
desks.rationale: Unrecorded repair risks become unexpected resale expenses.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Trace money stuck behind open jobs
desks.check: Pick service invoices or claims awaiting settlement; identify the missing approval, document or owner and expected clearance date.
desks.metric: Value of service receivables outstanding over 30 days (INR)
desks.rationale: A repaired vehicle does not create usable cash until the billing and collection loop closes.

issues.huddleTitle: Five desks. Five exceptions. Fifteen minutes.
issues.huddleSummary: Each function brings one real case with an incomplete handoff. Record the blocker, next action, owner and deadline in a shared log; recheck the same five cases tomorrow.
huddle: Minutes 0–3 — Sales: find one delivery with incomplete service onboarding; assign a callback.
Minutes 3–6 — Service: select one delayed or repeat RO; name the next action and customer-update time.
Minutes 6–9 — Spares: confirm a blocked repair part and realistic ETA, or document that none is available.
Minutes 9–12 — Used Cars: identify one appraisal with an unresolved diagnostic or repair-cost risk.
Minutes 12–15 — Accounts: take one ageing claim or invoice; assign its resolution owner and deadline.
limitations: This is a single commercial-vehicle manufacturer's announcement, not a representative measure of India's passenger-vehicle or two-wheeler aftersales market.

The platform scale of over 200,000 customers and more than 460,000 connected vehicles is company-reported as of the 13 October 2026 announcement; it has no disclosed monthly measurement window or independent audit.
The release provides no independently verified before/after result for workshop turnaround, first-time-right repair or customer satisfaction; do not claim such improvements are proven.
No vehicle wholesale, dealer retail-registration or market-share figures are used in this issue. The five suggested checks and metrics are RPHV editorial recommendations, not OEM benchmarks.
Technician safety, authorisations and vehicle-specific diagnosis must follow manufacturer documentation and applicable regulations; AI-generated advice is not a substitute.

metrics.context: July–September 2026 • SIAM

issues.reportingType: OEM-to-dealer domestic sales (wholesale); not retail registrations
intro: A strong market headline is a starting point, not a dealership performance report. On 15 October 2026, SIAM reported 13,60,687 passenger-vehicle domestic sales for the July–September quarter, 30.7% higher than the corresponding period of FY2025–26.

Those numbers describe manufacturer domestic dispatches—commonly called wholesales. Customer retail registrations are a separate measure. A dealership can see healthy vehicle inflow while still carrying excess stock, facing delayed deliveries or struggling to convert enquiries into invoices.

For the operations team, the right response is not to celebrate or panic on one industry number. It is to reconcile the market signal with the dealership's own pipeline, workshop load, inventory exposure and collection cycle.

interpretation.heading: What this means on the ground
points: Compare confirmed customer orders and registrations with new arrivals rather than treating dispatches as retail demand.
Review ageing units and delivery readiness before accepting that higher inventory automatically improves sales.
Connect expected vehicle parc growth with technician readiness, genuine parts supply and service retention—but do not infer service demand directly from one quarter's wholesales.

desks.name: SALES
desks.headline: Check delivery readiness, not just bookings
desks.check: Take the next seven days' booked deliveries. Confirm allocation, finance clearance, accessories, promised date and registration progress.
desks.metric: Delivery-ready bookings ÷ bookings due in 7 days (%)
desks.rationale: A booking is not yet a delivered car. Measure the handover pipeline.

desks.name: SERVICE
desks.headline: Make promised delivery dates visible
desks.check: Review all open repair orders with their promised completion times. Identify jobs blocked by diagnosis, approvals, parts or capacity.
desks.metric: ROs delivered within promise ÷ total delivered ROs (%)
desks.rationale: Customer confidence depends on reliable service completion, not only inflow.

desks.name: SPARES
desks.headline: Expose cash sitting in ageing stock
desks.check: List parts untouched for 90 days, then check demand, supersession, reservations and return possibilities before reordering.
desks.metric: Value of stock aged 90+ days ÷ total stock value (%)
desks.rationale: A growing market is not a reason to relax inventory discipline.

desks.name: USED CARS
desks.headline: Protect margin before acquisition
desks.check: For each proposed exchange, record ownership checks, repair inspection, reconditioning estimate and realistic resale value.
desks.metric: Acquisitions with approved margin sheet ÷ total acquisitions (%)
desks.rationale: Purchase price alone is not the acquisition cost.

desks.name: ACCOUNTS
desks.headline: Reconcile blocked money daily
desks.check: Trace unmatched receipts, delayed customer balances and pending manufacturer credits to a named owner and an expected resolution date.
desks.metric: Unreconciled receipts and claims older than 7 days (count)
desks.rationale: Turnover improves financial health only when cash and claims are controlled.

issues.huddleTitle: One blocked item. One owner. One deadline.
issues.huddleSummary: Each desk brings one exception that is holding up a delivery, repair, payment or stock decision. Close the huddle with a named owner and next action.
huddle: Minutes 0–3: Sales identifies one promised delivery at risk and checks the evidence.
Minutes 3–6: Service identifies one repair order that may miss its promise.
Minutes 6–9: Spares identifies one order or item whose status is unclear.
Minutes 9–12: Used Cars or Accounts identifies one margin or collection exception.
Minutes 12–15: Assign one owner and deadline to every unresolved exception.
limitations: SIAM's July–September PV domestic-sales data exclude BMW, Mercedes, JLR and Volvo Auto, as indicated in the release notes.
Wholesale dispatches do not equal customer retail registrations, and neither measure establishes any individual dealer's profitability.
The five department checks and suggested metrics are RPHV editorial recommendations, not published SIAM benchmarks.
